Kirloskar Oil Engines Ltd vs Rishabh Fashion India(P) Ltd on 1 October, 2007
IN THE STATE COMMISSION:DELHI
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 

 

  

 

  

 

 IN THE STATE COMMISSION: DELHI

of The Consumer

1. Whether Reporters of local newspapers
be allowed to see the judgment?
2. To be referred to the Reporter or not?
Justice J.D. Kapoor, President (Oral)
1. Respondent
is running a department store in Sant Nagar, Burari. Since there was erratic power supply by the
Delhi Vidyut Board, he purchased two generator sets of different kws. from the
appellant at the cost of Rs. 1,80,000/- and Rs.2,40,960/-. The said generator sets carried a warranty of
one year. The generator set started
giving trouble from the very next day of installation. It is alleged that the appellant never cared
to attend to the problem and so much so was unable to rectify the snags. On 7th March,
 2001 when
the respondent started the set, the engine
of generator set bursted and almost all parts of the engine and alternator were
damaged. Inspite of this no set was
replaced and some broken accessories/parts were removed by respondent-1. The performance of the generator set was
deteriorated and went out of order. Consequently, he filed the instant complaint
for refund of the cost of generator sets on account of business loss.
2. While
allowing the complaint the District Forum has vide impugned order dated
30.09.2003 directed the appellant to refund the aforesaid cost with interest @
9% and pay Rs. 2,000/- as cost of litigation.
Feeling aggrieved the appellant has preferred this appeal.
3. The
impugned order has been assailed firstly, on the ground that the appellant
being the manufacturer of the generator set was proceeded ex-parte and not given an opportunity of being heard
secondly, that the respondent-1 dealt with the dealer independently who was not
their dealer and did not purchase the set from the appellant and did not verify that the appellant was indeed
the authorized dealer and whether the
appellant was at all the manufacturer of any DG set, thirdly, that the respondent-1
fitted a different type of alternator viz. Stamford and there was mis-match
between the diesel engine of the appellant fitted in the DG set and the
alternator which was of a different make and lastly that the District Forum did
not obtain any expert opinion about mis-matching and manufacturing defect in
the DG set. Only expert engineer could have ascertained whether the
DG set was having some manufacturing defect.
5. In
our view none of the aforesaid contentions holds water. Once goods have a brand name a consumer is not expected to open
up each and every part to see whether it
bears stamford branded
name or not. The perusal of the impugned
order shows that engineers of the appellant had visited and had seen generator
set on some occasions and found some defect but they could not rectify. It was only after the burst that some parts were
destroyed in the process.
6. It is a misconceived notion that unless and until new goods
suffers from inherent manufacturing defect it cannot be held defective for the
purpose of replacement or for the purpose of refund of the cost or for the
purpose of refund of compensation as to the actual loss or injury suffered by
the consumer for the mental agony. The
quality and standard of every goods much less the branded new goods has to be
tested on the anvil of the definition of a word defect provided by
section 2(1)(f)
of the Consumer
Protection Act which means any fault, imperfection or shortcoming in the
quality, quantity, potency, purity or standard which is required to be
maintained by or under any law for the time being in force or (under any
contract, express or implied or} as is claimed by the trader in any manner
whatsoever in relation to any good.
7. If
a consumer after purchasing the branded new article starts visiting the dealer for
the service time and again and every
second or third day for removing one or other defects and if the job cards show
several defects, goods has to be held as
defective. It is not for the consumer to
engage an expert or engineer or some other expert to verify whether the goods
have manufacturing defect or not. He is a wronged person and to expect him to
incur unnecessary expenses in availing the services of an expert is too
much. The onus lies upon the trader or
manufacturer to show that their goods did not suffer from manufacturing
defect.
8. We
even go to the extent that even if the
manufacturer has a report in his favour that the goods does not have a
manufacturing defect, still he cannot escape
from the liability to compensate the consumer by
supplying defective goods and in terms of
Section 14(1)(d)
every
consumer is entitled to an amount as compensation as to the injury or actual
loss suffered by him due to the negligence of the opposite party. The word injury has a wide connotation in
terms of every remedy in the context of every contract. It was with an object to
inculcate high standard of quality or standard of the goods and the
efficiency in the service to be provided by the service provider that the
legislature defined the word defect in
a manner that any kind of fault or imperfection or shortcoming in the quality,
quantity, potency, purity or standards which is required to be maintained by or
under any law for the time being in force or under any contract, express or
implied or as is claimed by the trader in any manner whatsoever in relation to
any goods renders the goods defective.
9. Taking
over all view of the matter and finding
of fact returned by the District Forum as to the generator set having been
highly defective, the interest awarded by the District Forum in our view was not awardable because
interest is awardable only in those cases where there is a term of contract
between the parties or where there are equitable grounds. We have taken a view that ordinarily interest should be awarded in cases like fixed
deposits or by way of lump sum payment running into lacs towards purchase of
land or flats or wrongful rejection of insurance claims and not in those cases where the goods have been
sold against consideration and have been used by the consumer reluctantly or grudgingly.
10. In
the result, we partly allow the appeal by retaining the order for refund of the
cost of the generator set and
substituting the interest by lump sum compensation of Rs. 20,000/- which shall include the
cost of litigation.
11. The aforesaid payment shall be made
within one month from the date of receipt of this order.
12. Bank
Guarantee/FDR if any, furnished by the appellant, be returned forthwith.
13. A
copy of this order as per the statutory requirements be forwarded to the
parties free of charge and also to the concerned District Forum and thereafter
the file be consigned to Record room.
14. Announced
on 1st day of October, 2007.
(Justice J.D. Kapoor)
